claims.claim: In 2024 Japan picked three projects planning to store about 10 million tonnes of CO2 a year off Malaysia.
claims.source: JOGMEC, selection announcement dated 28 June 2024, and accompanying project descriptions: https://www.jogmec.go.jp/news/release/release_01181.html and https://www.jogmec.go.jp/content/300390539.pdf.
claims.correction: Accurate as a historical description of selected proposals. The three proposed capacities total 9.9–10.9 million tonnes annually. Selection did not establish contracted throughput, operating capacity or completed investment decisions.
claims.stale_check: The explicit 2024 date is appropriate. Subsequent programme developments should supplement, rather than invalidate, this historical statement.

claims.claim: No tonne has shipped
claims.source: No primary record establishing zero Japan-to-Malaysia CCS shipments through 18 November 2026 was located. Japan's April 2026 National Inventory Document covers historical activity through FY2024: https://cger.nies.go.jp/publications/report/i179/i179.pdf, section 3.4.1.2.
claims.correction: Remove the categorical zero-volume assertion unless supported by a current regulator or operator statement. Future project injection dates and historical absence of ship transport do not independently establish zero shipments through publication.
claims.stale_check: Neither Japan's inventory ending FY2024 nor the cited April 2026 reporting establishes the position on 18 November 2026.

claims.claim: no Japan–Malaysia agreement is signed.
claims.source: Malaysia Ministry of Economy, 17 October 2025 ministerial statement: https://ekonomi.gov.my/sites/default/files/2025-10/Media_Statement_The_3rd_Asia_Zero_Emission_Community_171025.pdf. Ministry's 15 September 2026 update: https://myccus.ekonomi.gov.my/activities/.
claims.correction: A government-to-government CCS Memorandum of Cooperation was signed on 17 October 2025. Distinguish that instrument from the operational cross-border agreement or arrangement required for CO2 transfers. The latest explicit ministry update located said those bilateral arrangements were being finalised on 15 September 2026; their signature status on 18 November remains unverified.
claims.stale_check: The cooperation memorandum predates the analysis by more than a year. The separate operational arrangement could also have progressed after September 2026.

claims.claim: Two sites lie off Peninsular Malaysia, under the 2025 federal CCUS Act.
claims.source: JOGMEC project appendix, 2024: https://www.jogmec.go.jp/content/300390539.pdf. Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, section 2 and Part VI: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: Accurate as a geographic and statutory-scope description. It does not establish that either project holds all required operating approvals.

claims.claim: Sarawak regulates the third under its own 2023 ordinance.
claims.source: Sarawak Environment (Reduction of Greenhouse Gases Emission) Ordinance 2023, gazetted 22 December 2023, section 3 and First Schedule: https://lawnet.sarawak.gov.my/lawnet_file/Ordinance/ORD_Cap.%2085%20ENVIRONMENT%20%28REDUCTION%20OF%20GREENHOUSE%20GASES%20EMISSION%29%20ORD%202023%20LawNet%202024%201.pdf.
claims.correction: The ordinance covers relevant offshore CCS activities, but it is only part of Sarawak's framework. Section 3(3) expressly requires reading it with the Land (Carbon Storage) Rules 2022 where applicable. Do not imply the ordinance alone supplies storage licensing and post-closure rules.

claims.claim: On 23 Oct 2026 Petronas, TotalEnergies and Mitsui signed a joint venture for a CO2 storage hub off Peninsular Malaysia's east coast: up to 5 million tonnes a year, first injection as early as 2031.
claims.source: PETRONAS original announcement, independently checked, 23 October 2026: https://www.petronas.com/media/media-releases/petronas-totalenergies-and-mitsui-sign-joint-venture-agreement-develop-carbon. Bernama's corresponding report: https://web26.bernama.com/bm/news.php?id=2624493. Geographic connection: JOGMEC 2024 project appendix.
claims.correction: Prefer 'signed a joint venture agreement'. The named signatories were PETRONAS CCS Ventures, TotalEnergies EP CCS Malaysia and Mitsui. The agreement provides a framework for forming a dedicated company. Capacity and first injection remain phase-one expectations, conditional on readiness.
claims.stale_check: Confirmed against the October 2026 announcement; this supersedes earlier project timing assumptions.

claims.claim: The hub 'is being developed to receive CO2 domestically and regionally, including potential cross-border CO2 shipments', so its 5 Mtpa is hub capacity, not Japanese tonnes.
claims.source: PETRONAS announcement and independently checked Bernama report, 23 October 2026: https://www.petronas.com/media/media-releases/petronas-totalenergies-and-mitsui-sign-joint-venture-agreement-develop-carbon and https://web26.bernama.com/bm/news.php?id=2624493.
claims.correction: The distinction is justified. No reviewed source assigns all five million tonnes annually to Japanese customers.

claims.claim: It is one of three Malaysian sites on Japan's 2024 list
claims.source: JOGMEC project appendix, 2024: https://www.jogmec.go.jp/content/300390539.pdf. Malaysia Ministry of Economy statement identifying the Southern Offshore Peninsular Malaysia partners, 17 October 2025: https://ekonomi.gov.my/sites/default/files/2025-10/Media_Statement_The_3rd_Asia_Zero_Emission_Community_171025.pdf.
claims.correction: Prefer 'corresponds to the Southern Offshore Peninsular Malaysia project on the 2024 list'. A hub or project can encompass multiple storage areas; the sources do not establish a one-to-one identity between a single reservoir and every later development component.

claims.claim: its investment decision is pending.
claims.source: PETRONAS announcement, 23 October 2026: https://www.petronas.com/media/media-releases/petronas-totalenergies-and-mitsui-sign-joint-venture-agreement-develop-carbon, independently checked against Bernama's same-day report.
claims.correction: Specify 'the final investment decision remained ahead of the project in the 23 October announcement'.
claims.stale_check: No later official FID announcement was located, but the directly verified status is dated 23 October 2026.

claims.claim: METI's 2024 list names no Petronas company for the Southern project ('closely working with Petronas and TotalEnergies'); Petronas CCS Ventures later signed the JV.
claims.source: JOGMEC's corresponding official 2024 appendix, page 3: https://www.jogmec.go.jp/content/300390539.pdf. PETRONAS announcement, 23 October 2026: https://www.petronas.com/media/media-releases/petronas-totalenergies-and-mitsui-sign-joint-venture-agreement-develop-carbon.
claims.correction: Accurate distinction between the listed project companies and collaborators. Absence from that company column must not be presented as absence of PETRONAS involvement in 2024.

claims.claim: JOGMEC selected nine Advanced CCS Projects on 28 Jun 2024 that 'aim to store approximately 20 Mtpa of CO2 in total', five in Japan and four in the Asia-Pacific
claims.source: JOGMEC Japanese announcement, 28 June 2024: https://www.jogmec.go.jp/news/release/release_01181.html. English announcement, 24 July 2024, revised 5 September 2024: https://www.jogmec.go.jp/english/news/release/release_00268.html.
claims.correction: The nine-project portfolio, approximate aggregate and domestic/overseas split are supported. These were selected development proposals.
claims.stale_check: The selection date is 28 June; the English release's publication date is 24 July. Keep those dates distinct.

claims.claim: Northern Offshore Peninsular about 3 Mtpa, evaluated as 'promising but further initial studies were required'
claims.source: JOGMEC project appendix, 2024, pages 2–3: https://www.jogmec.go.jp/content/300390539.pdf.
claims.correction: Accurate as the 2024 evaluation.
claims.stale_check: Do not present this historical qualification as a verified November 2026 stage-gate result.

claims.claim: Offshore Sarawak about 1.9 to 2.9 Mtpa; Southern Offshore Peninsular about 5 Mtpa
claims.source: JOGMEC project appendix, 2024, page 3: https://www.jogmec.go.jp/content/300390539.pdf.
claims.correction: Both proposed capacities match. The Southern entry explicitly identifies the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia.
claims.stale_check: Historical proposal capacities, not verified current throughput.

claims.claim: Sum about 9.9 to 10.9 Mtpa (FORA arithmetic), planned capacities, not contracts.
claims.source: Independent arithmetic using JOGMEC's 2024 primary figures: https://www.jogmec.go.jp/content/300390539.pdf.
claims.correction: 3 + 1.9–2.9 + 5 = 9.9–10.9. The qualification about planned capacity is essential.

claims.claim: Japan's own 2030 goal is 6 to 12 Mtpa of storage.
claims.source: JOGMEC official English release, 24 July 2024, revised 5 September 2024: https://www.jogmec.go.jp/english/news/release/release_00268.html.
claims.correction: Identify this as the government target reported in the 2024 programme announcement. An indexed METI English explanatory page returned a conflicting six-to-eight formulation, but its text could not be opened; the explicit Japanese and English project-selection releases support six to twelve and are preferred.
claims.stale_check: No primary evidence establishing a replacement target was located. The 2024 target does not guarantee individual projects' current schedules.

claims.claim: AP's 'by 2030 ... 20 million tons' conflates the two
claims.source: AP article, 17 February 2026, syndicated at https://www.thehour.com/news/world/article/malaysia-and-japan-plan-major-cross-border-carbon-21357693.php; underlying JOGMEC announcement independently checked: https://www.jogmec.go.jp/english/news/release/release_00268.html.
claims.correction: The alleged conflation is not established. AP assigns the figure to nine sites; JOGMEC itself combines that portfolio with a 2030 programme ambition. Criticising certainty about prospective delivery is more defensible than asserting that AP confused the two figures.
claims.stale_check: AP's February article predates the Southern Hub's October 2026 announcement of first injection as early as 2031.

claims.claim: Kasawari CCS (3.3 Mtpa, first injection target 2027) stores domestic CO2 and is not part of the Japanese projects.
claims.source: PETRONAS original project announcement, 29 November 2022: https://www.petronas.com/bm/node/1155. Bernama, 1 April 2026: https://www.bernamabiz.com/news.php?id=2539728. Sarawak government's UKAS report, 26 August 2026: https://ukas.sarawak.gov.my/web/subpage/news_view/47328. JOGMEC 2024 project appendix.
claims.correction: The domestic project identity and planned 3.3-million-tonne annual reduction are supported. The timetable is unresolved: April reporting describes an early-stage attempt to bring injection forward to 2027 from 2029 or 2030; August's official state report says 2028. An older indexed PETRONAS page says 2026 but could not be reopened. Do not select a settled current target without an updated operator confirmation.
claims.stale_check: The analysis uses an April aspiration without the newer August statement. UKAS is newer and governmental, but its speaker is not the operator, so 2028 should be attributed rather than treated as definitive.

claims.claim: Kasawari's '1% of Petronas emissions' holds only with Scope 3 included; ~6% of Scope 1+2
claims.source: PETRONAS 2025 sustainability data, accessed 18 November 2026: https://www.petronas.com/sustainability/sustainability-performance-data. Earlier results release, 27 February 2026: https://www.petronas.com/media/media-releases/petronas-posts-lower-profit-amid-market-headwinds-strengthens-resilience.
claims.correction: Specify year and boundary. Using disclosed 2025 operational-control data, 3.3/55.57 = 5.94%; adding Scope 3 categories 1 and 11 gives 3.3/(55.57+18.73+300.03) = 0.882%. These compare planned abatement with historical emissions. The earlier release gives 56.95 rather than 55.57; the current detailed table is preferred, but the particular revision was not explained in the material reviewed.
claims.stale_check: The earlier and later company figures differ, although both round the operational-emissions comparison to about six percent.

claims.claim: Malaysia's 2025 CCUS Act names the Government as payer of a closed offshore site's long-term care, from a fund whose levy may not be raised when the fund is drawn down.
claims.source: Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, sections 30–32 and 41–42: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: Government stewardship follows a qualifying transfer. The levy restriction concerns increases because of withdrawals, not all increases after withdrawals.

claims.claim: In March 2025 then economy minister Rafizi Ramli was reported as saying the government 'will not bear any costs' of CCUS projects.
claims.source: Dewan Rakyat Hansard, 6 March 2025, printed pages 52–57, parliamentary document available through CLJ's mirror: https://cljlaw.com/files/hansard/DR/pdf/DR-06032025.pdf. Official Dewan Negara Hansard, 25 March 2025, pages 137–138: https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/hindex/pdf/DN-25032025.pdf.
claims.correction: The historical attribution is supported, but the juxtaposition needs context. Rafizi described private infrastructure financing and also explicitly acknowledged later government expenditure funded by the levy trust fund. Do not imply that he denied government's post-transfer role.
claims.stale_check: This is a March 2025 statement, not a current ministerial position. The official-host March 6 PDF failed to load; the inspected document is a parliamentary transcript mirrored by CLJ.

claims.claim: The levy still has no gazetted rate.
claims.source: AGC Laws of Malaysia Act 870 index, searched 18 November 2026: https://lom.agc.gov.my/. Section 30's gazettement requirement was checked in the official Act: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: No levy order was identified, but an exhaustive live gazette check was not obtainable. Use 'No gazetted injection-levy rate was identified in the official records reviewed as of 18 November 2026.'
claims.stale_check: A negative legal-status assertion requires a contemporaneous complete register or regulator confirmation.

claims.claim: AGC lists to 18 Nov 2026 show no levy order and no import regulations
claims.source: AGC Act 870 index, searched 18 November 2026: https://lom.agc.gov.my/. The retrieved indexed listing showed the Act, P.U.(B) 355/2025 and P.U.(A) 346/2025; direct access to the full listing failed.
claims.correction: The retrieved listing is consistent with the assertion, but it does not conclusively certify absence. Report the bounded search result and retain verification of both instruments as an outstanding publication check.
claims.stale_check: The June draft workshop cannot establish that import regulations remained ungazetted in November.

claims.claim: draft in June 2026
claims.source: Ministry of Economy/MyCCUS, workshop entry dated 22 June 2026: https://myccus.ekonomi.gov.my/activities/.
claims.correction: The workshop concerned draft import-permit and registration regulations.
claims.stale_check: Verified for June only.

claims.claim: Act 870 s. 32(1): once a storage site is closed, 'the obligations relating to monitoring, corrective measures and remediation measures shall be transferred to the Government'
claims.source: Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, sections 31–32: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: The quotation is accurate. Closure alone does not trigger transfer.

claims.claim: s. 32(2): only after 'a prescribed period has lapsed from the issuance of the closure certificate' and prescribed conditions are met
claims.source: Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, section 32(2): https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: Accurate; the implementing regulation is now directly verified.

claims.claim: s. 32(3): the operator keeps 'criminal, contractual or civil law liability ... attributable to the fault, negligence or deceit of the offshore operator'
claims.source: Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, section 32(3): https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: Add failure to exercise due diligence when describing the complete exclusion.

claims.claim: s. 41(2): the Post-Closure Stewardship Fund holds Government sums, the injection levy ('financial support to the Government') and investment income.
claims.source: Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, section 41(2): https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: These are statutory funding sources, not verified receipts or balances.

claims.claim: s. 42(1): the Fund pays 'costs to be borne by the Government for long-term stewardship of offshore storage sites after the transfer of obligations'
claims.source: Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, section 42(1): https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: Accurate.

claims.claim: the Act does not cap the Government's exposure at the Fund balance.
claims.source: Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, particularly sections 32 and 41–42: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: Identify this as textual interpretation, not an express unlimited-liability provision.

claims.claim: s. 30(2)(b): the levy 'shall not be increased due to withdrawals from the Fund or risks associated with other offshore storage projects'
claims.source: Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, section 30(2)(b): https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: The exact statutory quotation is accurate.

claims.claim: s. 30(3)(a): the Agency 'may review' rates every five years.
claims.source: Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, section 30(3): https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: Accurate; review remains subject to subsection 30(2).

claims.claim: a minimum of 10 years after the closure certificate before transfer, extendable
claims.source: P.U.(A) 346/2025, gazetted 30 September 2025, regulations 42–44: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/3100038/PUA%20346%20%282025%29.pdf.
claims.correction: Now verified directly. For the standard operator-requested route, transfer requires at least ten years, containment evidence, paid levies, sealing, decommissioning and seabed/subsoil restoration. Regulation 44 permits extension. The separate licence-revocation route should not automatically be described as having the same ten-year minimum.
claims.stale_check: This rule has applied since October 2025. The original analysis disclosed a research gap; the gap is now resolved.

claims.claim: P.U.(A) 346/2025 (in force 1 Oct 2025)
claims.source: P.U.(A) 346/2025, 30 September 2025, regulation 1(2): https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/3100038/PUA%20346%20%282025%29.pdf.
claims.correction: The commencement date is correct. 'Only' should mean only substantive regulations identified in the reviewed index, since a separate commencement instrument also exists.

claims.claim: Commencement: AGC gives 1 Oct 2025 (P.U.(B) 355/2025)
claims.source: P.U.(B) 355/2025, dated 30 September 2025: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/3100047/PUB355_2025.pdf.
claims.correction: Add 'except Part VII', concerning onshore assessment and storage. The notification expressly excludes that Part.
claims.stale_check: The Act's 1 August 2025 gazette publication date is distinct from commencement.

claims.claim: one law-firm note says 1 Aug 2025 (publication date).
claims.source: The unnamed law-firm note was not identified. The official Act confirms publication on 1 August 2025, while P.U.(B) 355/2025 confirms commencement on 1 October except Part VII: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/3100047/PUB355_2025.pdf.
claims.correction: Retain the verified publication/commencement distinction. Remove or identify the alleged erroneous note.

claims.claim: Rafizi's '20 to 30 years' is a site-contract term, not a post-closure period
claims.source: Dewan Rakyat Hansard, 6 March 2025, printed page 56: https://cljlaw.com/files/hansard/DR/pdf/DR-06032025.pdf. Dewan Negara Hansard, 25 March 2025, printed page 137: https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/hindex/pdf/DN-25032025.pdf.
claims.correction: The correction is sound. Neither passage establishes a mandatory 20–30-year period after closure.
claims.stale_check: These March statements preceded the October 2025 implementing regulations.

claims.claim: he has since left the post
claims.source: March 2025 Hansard identifies Rafizi as economy minister; P.U.(B) 355/2025, 30 September 2025, identifies Amir Hamzah as minister; 12 November 2026 parliamentary proceedings identify Akmal Nasrullah: https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/hindex/pdf/DN-25032025.pdf, https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/3100047/PUB355_2025.pdf and https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-rakyat/2026-11-12.
claims.correction: 'Then economy minister' is appropriate. No exact resignation date is needed.
claims.stale_check: Verified against later official records.

claims.claim: Under Malaysia's federal law, its last chapter is a public bill: a sealed reservoir the Government pays to watch.
claims.source: Act 870, sections 32 and 41–42, 1 August 2025; parliamentary committee report DN3/2025, 19 March 2025, paragraph 55: https://parlimen.gov.my/ipms/eps/2025-03-19/DN.3.2025%20-%20DN3.2025.pdf.
claims.correction: Government-borne stewardship costs are real. An inevitable unfunded taxpayer shortfall is not established. Describe potential residual public exposure and the funding provisions.
claims.stale_check: The concern survives verification; the rhetorical implication needs narrowing.

claims.claim: It is like agreeing to take back a sealed storeroom for good once the tenant moves out
claims.source: P.U.(A) 346/2025, 30 September 2025, regulations 32–33 and 41–44: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/3100038/PUA%20346%20%282025%29.pdf.
claims.correction: The embedded premise compresses a conditional transfer into apparent immediate handover. Preserve the intervening operator duties, financial security and transfer requirements.
claims.stale_check: These protections were already in force before the analysis.

claims.claim: before anyone has set the fee that pays for its upkeep.
claims.source: No complete primary register confirming absence of a levy order was obtainable as of 18 November 2026. AGC portal: https://lom.agc.gov.my/.
claims.correction: This depends on the unresolved gazette-absence assertion. Say the rate was not located in reviewed records, rather than asserting that nobody has set it.
claims.stale_check: Requires publication-date confirmation.

claims.claim: Malaysia's law already puts the long-term care of a closed site on the Government.
claims.source: Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, sections 31–32 and 42: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: Specify 'after a qualifying transfer of offshore-site obligations'.

claims.claim: Malaysia's CCUS Act 2025 lets CO2 captured abroad be imported for permanent storage.
claims.source: Act 870, gazetted 1 August 2025, sections 19–20 and 23: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.
claims.correction: Import requires an agency permit and compliant CO2 streams; this is not unconditional shipment authorisation.

claims.claim: Under UN climate-reporting guidance, the country that captures CO2 reports it as captured and exported. The country storing it reports any that escapes from the site.
claims.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Volume 2, Chapter 5, section 5.10, pages 5.20–5.21: https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2006gl/pdf/2_Volume2/V2_5_Ch5_CCS.pdf.
claims.correction: Accurate shorthand. The full rule also covers imports and emissions from transport, temporary storage and injection.
claims.stale_check: Chapter 5 was not refined in 2019.

claims.claim: captured CO2 is subtracted at source and later emissions from transport, injection and the reservoir 'should be counted in national total emissions'.
claims.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Volume 2, Chapter 2, section 2.3.4, equation 2.7 and pages 2.36–2.37: https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2006gl/pdf/2_Volume2/V2_2_Ch2_Stationary_Combustion.pdf.
claims.correction: Accurate for qualifying capture and geological storage. It does not by itself establish the accounting treatment of a particular future export transaction.

claims.claim: The 2019 Refinement made no change to Chapter 5.
claims.source: IPCC 2019 Refinement, Volume 2 contents: https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2019rf/vol2.html.
claims.correction: The official contents explicitly designate Chapter 5 as having no refinement.

claims.claim: These are inventory-reporting rules, not liability rules; they create no credit
claims.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Volume 2, Chapter 5, particularly section 5.10: https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2006gl/pdf/2_Volume2/V2_5_Ch5_CCS.pdf.
claims.correction: Prefer 'These guidelines do not themselves allocate financial liability or issue tradable carbon credits.' Separate crediting arrangements may exist.

claims.claim: how Japan's own inventory treats exported CO2 is not confirmed in any source opened.
claims.source: Japan's National Inventory Document 2026, April 2026: https://cger.nies.go.jp/publications/report/i179/i179.pdf.
claims.correction: The analyst's past research process cannot be independently audited. This review also did not establish a worked Japan-to-Malaysia export treatment. Keep the substantive uncertainty, without implying that Japan lacks applicable inventory rules.
claims.stale_check: The document's historical coverage cannot establish future transaction-level treatment.

claims.claim: If CO2 injected in one country leaks in another, 'Country A is responsible for reporting the emissions from the geological storage site'.
claims.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Volume 2, Chapter 5, pages 5.20–5.21: https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/2006gl/pdf/2_Volume2/V2_5_Ch5_CCS.pdf.
claims.correction: Country A means the injecting country in this separate example. Do not confuse it with the capturing country labelled A in the preceding example.

claims.claim: the fraction retained in appropriately selected and managed geological reservoirs is 'very likely to exceed 99% over 100 years and is likely to exceed 99% over 1,000 years'
claims.source: IPCC Special Report on Carbon Dioxide Capture and Storage, 2005, Summary for Policymakers, paragraph 25: https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/03/srccs_summaryforpolicymakers-1.pdf.
claims.correction: The quotation is accurate. In the short card, retain both selection and management conditions and identify the assessment year. It is not a site-specific guarantee.

omitted_facts: The federal regulations require financial security effective before injection and maintained through transfer. The regulator can require increases after assessing risks and costs. This protection is separate from the injection levy. Source: P.U.(A) 346/2025, 30 September 2025, regulations 14 and 32–33, https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/3100038/PUA%20346%20%282025%29.pdf.

Parliament's own March 2025 fiscal explanation acknowledges government funding for agency operations and describes the stewardship fund as reducing future dependence on government funds. This directly supports scrutiny of residual public exposure without implying that the government role was concealed. Source: Dewan Negara committee report DN3/2025, 19 March 2025, paragraph 55, https://parlimen.gov.my/ipms/eps/2025-03-19/DN.3.2025%20-%20DN3.2025.pdf.

Investment earnings from the federal stewardship fund may also support general development of the CCUS industry. Source: Act 870, 1 August 2025, section 42(2), https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2995040_BI/Act%20870%20CARBON%20CAPTURE%2C%20UTILIZATION%20AND%20STORAGE%20ACT%202025.pdf.

Sarawak's Land (Carbon Storage) Rules contain their own post-closure arrangements: a normally at-least-20-year period that can be reduced when specified conditions are satisfied, a financial contribution intended to cover estimated post-transfer costs, and recovery for operator fault. The federal ten-year rule should not be applied to Sarawak. Source: Swk. L.N. 349/2022, 22 December 2022, rules 41–43, https://lawnet.sarawak.gov.my/lawnet_file/Subsidiary/SUB_Issue%20No.%2084%20L.N.%20349%20Land%20Carbon%20Storage.pdf.

A CCS cooperation memorandum between Malaysia and Japan was already signed on 17 October 2025. Its existence does not establish that it satisfies every requirement for operational CO2 exports. Source: Ministry of Economy, https://ekonomi.gov.my/sites/default/files/2025-10/Media_Statement_The_3rd_Asia_Zero_Emission_Community_171025.pdf.

Japan has declared provisional application of the 2009 export amendment, which has not generally entered into force. Official sources disagree on the declaration date: IMO's 30 October 2026 book says 16 October 2025, while Japan MOFA's 8 April 2026 record says 16 December 2025. Both agree on acceptance on 16 December. IMO is the more recent depositary record, but the exact declaration-date conflict should remain unresolved without the underlying notification. Sources: https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/About/Conventions/StatusOfConventions/Status%202026%20-%20Vol.%20II.pdf and https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/ila/st/pagew_000001_00446.html.

An Article 6 arrangement can be non-binding, including an MoU, provided the substantive requirements are satisfied. The exporting contracting state also retains accountability for Protocol compliance when exporting to a non-party. Malaysia's domestic stewardship allocation therefore does not describe the entire international responsibility framework. Source: IMO guidance, 21 October 2013, Annex 6, sections 2.1 and 3.2, https://www.umweltbundesamt.de/sites/default/files/medien/381/dokumente/london_protocol-lc_35-15-_report_of_the_thirty-fifth_consultative_meeting_and_the_eight_meeting_of_the_contracting_parties.pdf.

JOGMEC selected six emitter clusters as prospective contractors in June 2026 to reduce ship-based CCS costs through aggregation and shared facilities. It continued transport and storage studies. These six clusters should not be confused with the nine projects selected in 2024. Source: JOGMEC, 24 June 2026, https://www.jogmec.go.jp/english/news/release/release_00446.html.

The minister told Parliament on 12 November 2026 that two offshore assessment permits had been issued to PETRONAS applicants by September, with initial hub development focused on Kuantan. Assessment permits are not storage-operation licences or shipment approvals. Source: official digital Hansard, marked draft, https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-rakyat/2026-11-12.

The IPCC's 2022 assessment provides more recent scientific context: appropriately selected and managed geological storage can permanently isolate CO2, while implementation faces technical, economic and institutional barriers. This does not verify any particular Malaysian reservoir. Source: IPCC AR6 Working Group III, 2022, SPM C.4.6, https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg3/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGIII_Full_Report.pdf.
source_assessment: The supplied analysis contains 16 distinct bracketed source identifiers, plus additional unlabelled and bundled references. The exact number of unique underlying documents cannot be reconstructed from those labels alone because several entries combine institutions, publications or dates without URLs. The source base includes Malaysian and Japanese government material, Sarawak legislation, international technical and treaty bodies, industry announcements, commercial legal commentary, and reporting containing environmental criticism. That is substantial institutional breadth, but it is not demonstrably a full political or stakeholder spectrum. Direct opposition, affected-community, independent reservoir-risk and fiscal-cost evidence is limited or absent. Several news reports repeat the same company announcement, and multiple legal summaries repeat the same legislation; these are not independent primary confirmations. The diversity estimate is a qualitative editorial judgement, not a calculated statistic. All four cardinal categories were assessed. No separate UNDERCLAIM is independently substantiated: resolving the openly disclosed ten-year-regulation gap strengthens the research without making the earlier disclosure false.
overall_assessment: Reviewed against records available on 18 November 2026, the analysis has a sound central statutory proposition and largely accurate project-capacity and inventory-reporting facts. Its strongest point is that qualifying offshore stewardship obligations eventually pass to government under federal law. Its weakest points are categorical current-status negatives, compressed liability framing, and insufficient separation between dated statements and present conditions. Before publication, distinguish the signed 2025 cooperation memorandum from the unresolved operational cross-border arrangement; qualify the zero-shipment and ungazetted-rate assertions; replace secondary descriptions of the ten-year rule with the regulation itself; preserve operator financial security and transfer conditions; contextualise Rafizi's remarks and the 2005 IPCC liability quotation; and remove the unsupported accusation that AP conflated the two targets. Kasawari timing also needs an updated operator confirmation. The 78/100 score is an overall editorial reliability assessment, not the arithmetic mean of the belief masses. UNVERIFIED findings indicate evidence limits, not findings of falsity. Repeated propositions are consolidated, and policy recommendations are not treated as independently testable facts.
